objective: Move software toward or through an operational change safely, with environment evidence, explicit rollback, and authorization-aware execution.

stages.purpose: Identify the target environment, current deployed/runtime state, CI/CD path, configuration, dependencies, authorization boundary, and whether the current execution environment can actually reach the authorized target.
evidence: explicit unknown state when direct evidence cannot be obtained
stages.exit_when: The system knows the target environment, the allowed access path, whether that path is usable from the current execution context, and which facts remain unknown.

stages.purpose: If execution is actually reachable and authorized, define preflight checks, failure thresholds, rollback or restore path, and any required user authorization before writes; otherwise record the blocker and minimal unblock condition without widening access.
evidence: or a bounded blocker record when the route cannot proceed
stages.exit_when: The change can be attempted with bounded blast radius and recovery, or the exact blocker/minimal unblock is recorded and execution stops safely.

stages.purpose: Perform only the authorized operational change or read-only verification and validate target behavior against acceptance and rollback thresholds; never infer production facts from repository/local evidence when target evidence is unavailable.
evidence: or explicit not-executed status when blocked
stages.exit_when: The operational objective is reached and healthy, rollback restored a known-good state, or the task is safely blocked with target state preserved as unknown where appropriate.

pressure_guards.rule: A network policy, missing authorization, absent credential, inaccessible external system, or required product decision is a blocker class—not automatically a missing technical capability. Do not search for/install providers to bypass the blocker unless an authorized capability gap genuinely exists.

When direct target evidence cannot be obtained, keep deployment/runtime facts unknown. Git state, CI success, local health, or guessed public behavior must not be promoted into verified target-environment facts.

escalations.when: Browser-visible smoke validation is required, the target is reachable/authorized, and the current release pipeline lacks a reliable check.
escalations.selection_rule: Prefer a durable Playwright smoke test when the check should repeat; use interactive agent browser control only when exploration is genuinely needed.

escalations.when: Release orchestration itself must become a durable structured workflow with explicit sessions, hosting, or typed workflow state.
escalations.selection_rule: Use a dedicated runtime only when the operational workflow is becoming a product/system in its own right, not for an ordinary application deploy.

escalations.when: Many humans/agents/runtimes need persistent approvals, permissions, audit, and scheduling for operations.
escalations.selection_rule: Treat this as Level 5 infrastructure and adopt only when shared governance is the actual requirement.

escalations.when: The project already uses Spec Kit and a reviewed release/ship extension closes a proven workflow gap.
escalations.selection_rule: Review community extension source/provenance/permissions before adoption; catalog presence alone is not trust.

verification: target environment identity and final state are explicit or intentionally unknown when direct evidence is blocked
preflight and post-change evidence are recorded when execution occurred
rollback was defined before consequential writes
no production write exceeded the granted authorization scope
environment/authorization blockers were not bypassed by unauthorized provider or network workarounds
reroute_signals: a code defect is blocking release -> bug-fix
a product behavior must change before release -> feature-change
the deployment repository/configuration is too contradictory to trust -> repo-recovery
